opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez (E046) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Requested write is within the full-time limit and at or below the requested level, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E046 is a contractor with basic training (note says full-time, but security record governs). Contractors max out at read without advanced training, so write to Payroll is not permitted. Recommend read.
reason: The requested level is write to Payroll. The HR note claims E046 is full-time, but the Security note states the security record (which governs) shows E046 is a contractor with basic security training, and explicitly flags that the full-time claim is incorrect. Per policy, contractors without advanced training max out at read. Since write exceeds the max, I grant the maximum of read.

Note 2 (Security): employment type contractor, security training basic, role Payroll Specialist, recommends read. Says contractors max out at read without advanced training, so write not permitted.

Conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor with basic training. The Security note claims the security record governs.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

The conflict is employment type: full_time vs contractor. Also security training.

If full_time: write allowed (Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, but write is within full-time limit; admin would require ownership, but requested is write). So grant write.

If contractor with basic training: max read. So grant read.
